description: 2nd order Butterworth low-pass (fc = 0.1), new style feedback taps, vs iir_filter_ffd

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 1.2348807196370536e-4 (times the input peak 0.705), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 4.146588791010113: <= 4.946046680690277 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q15 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 1.2348807196370536e-4 (times the input peak 0.705), and each output rounding (1.0 LSB of Q15, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 4.146588791010113: <= 7.019341076195333 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

Coefficients rounded to Q17 change the impulse response by ||dh||_1 = 2.917001615214012e-5 (times the input peak 0.705), and each output rounding (0.5 LSB of Q17, plus 0.02 Q15 LSB for the f32 reference) is shaped by the feedback 1/A(z), ||g||_1 = 4.146700151042047: <= 1.2122068968179518 Q15 LSB per component. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: GNU Radio keeps the state in double, this is f32: each step rounds the sum (terms of total size 1.4024719933130894) by 4 * 2^-24 at most, amplified by ||1/A(z)||_1 = 4.1466892179656325: 0.0454 Q15 LSB. SNR minimum is the measured value minus 1 dB.
